head.title: Two different businesses, one system underneath
head.aside: These aren't two products bundled together. It's one booking engine, one record and one reporting layer that change shape depending on the model you run — and you can run both at once.

rental.title: Traditional rental
rental.body: A booking's whole life sits in one record: rate, payment, additional drivers, signed agreement, check-out, return, inspection and audit trail. The counter stops being the bottleneck because the customer already did half of it from their phone.

loaners.title: Dealership loaners

head.title: From booking to closeout, without leaving the record
head.aside: Six stops. One timeline. Every event is written against the booking, so closeout doesn't depend on anyone remembering what happened at 9:15 AM.

0.body: The customer books by location and date. Staff can take over at any point without starting over.

1.body: Agreement signed, license verified, mileage and fuel recorded, keys handed over.

2.body: Check-out and check-in photos in the same record, compared side by side to decide whether there's damage.

3.body: AutoExpreso and SunPass crossings land against whichever booking held the unit at that hour.

4.body: Rate, extras, tolls and damage charges add up once, with nothing retyped.

5.body: Deposit released, unit returned to inventory with its next action, record sealed.

detail.title: One record, not seven tabs
detail.body: Most operators don't lose money on the rate — they lose it on what never got billed. A toll that showed up three weeks late. Damage nobody photographed. A deposit left on hold. The spine exists so those things have an owner and a timestamp.

0.title: Every event carries a time and a user
0.body: Disputes get settled by reading the log, not by anyone's memory.

1.title: Tolls find their own booking
1.body: A crossing matches by plate and timestamp, even when the statement arrives weeks later.

2.title: Closeout hands the unit back to the board
2.body: With its next action already assigned: wash, shop, or ready to hand over.

head.title: What it does today, and what we're building
head.aside: Anything carrying the Building tag has not shipped yet. We say it right here, on the same line as the claim, so nobody buys a demo of something that doesn't exist.

0.title: Let the customer arrive with half already done
0.body: Shorter counter queue, less paper, fewer calls asking for the license again.
A clean public storefront where the guest searches where and when. Your internal location and model structure stays hidden.

1.body: Pre-check-in, agreement signature and payment in one guided flow. The customer resumes where they left off, on any device.

2.body: Pick up outside counter hours, with identity verification and key handover without staff on site.

1.title: The whole shift from one phone
1.body: Handovers, returns, inspections and issues in one queue, not four WhatsApp groups.

0.body: A phone-first view where the shift reads as a task list: who's picking up, who's returning, what's missing.

1.body: Guided photo capture, a before/after compare packet and damage triage with a suggested next action.

2.body: Every complaint, dispute or incident becomes a case with an owner, a history and a status, instead of a message that gets lost.

2.title: Know which unit is ready, and why
2.body: Availability stops being a conversation and becomes a number you can audit.

0.body: Each unit shows what it's missing — wash, fuel, inspection, maintenance — and which signal says so. No black box.

1.body: Plans shortage, wash and maintenance with rules you set per location and per business model, not a generic average.

2.body: Rate adjustment against what the market charges, class by class and inside the caps you set. It runs with the Market Intelligence add-on; without it, rates follow your fixed rules for season, location and length of rental.

3.title: Bill what you already earned
3.body: Tolls, deposits, commissions and damage reconciled against the same booking.

0.value: Payments and deposits through multiple gateways
0.body: Hold at check-out, charges during the rental, release at closeout, on whichever gateway you already use. Payment state lives inside the record, not on another screen.

1.body: AutoExpreso, SunPass, E-PASS and FasTrak matched by plate and timestamp to the right booking, then billed to the driver who crossed.

2.body: Damage goes from inspection to insurer without leaving the system: the evidence, the triage and the claim file all live in one place.

bookings.title: Every booking, from every channel, in one place
bookings.lede: Reservations arrive from your franchise systems, your brokers, your own website and your counter, and land in a single queue, already matched to a customer, priced, and ready to hand over.

0.body: Franchise and broker reservations pull themselves in, match against the customers and vehicles you already have, and pass a duplicate check before they ever reach your staff.

1.value: The handover is a guided flow
1.body: Agreement, terms, payment, eight-angle photo inspection and signature, in order, from a tablet or a phone. The customer can do their part before they reach the counter.

2.body: Mileage, fuel, cleaning, late return and tolls are worked out at check-in, charged to the card on file where you hold a signed authorization, and receipted without anyone asking.

trust.title: The awkward cases are the ones that cost money
trust.body: An imported booking that does not match cleanly is never guessed at: it waits in a review tray, with what the system found, for a person to decide. A car returned with a balance owing gets its own status instead of being filed as closed. What usually gets papered over is what gets expensive, so here it does not.

items.0: Each franchise or broker connection is built for that partner. Six run in production today, and adding one is real work, not a switch.
items.1: Clean imports promote themselves and ambiguous ones go to review. That is the feature, not a limitation.
items.2: Charging the card on file rests on the authorization the customer signed on the agreement, which names the categories: fuel, mileage, cleaning, tolls and damage.
items.3: Pre-check-in, digital signature and the customer portal are real, but someone still hands over a key unless you run a kiosk.

bookings.proof: As of August 2026: seven rental operations and more than four thousand reservations moved in the last thirty days.

university.title: Your team learns the software by doing the work, not by watching a video
university.lede: Eleven guided modules inside the product, across four courses. Four of them cannot be passed by reading: they close when the person does the real work and the server confirms it against the operation's own records.

0.value: Learned by doing, not by watching
0.body: The modules for creating a booking, handing a car over, taking it back and recording a payment complete themselves the next time that person actually does it. There is no I-have-read-this button: the server goes looking for the record.

1.value: It never asks for pretend work
1.body: No module asks anyone to create a booking or record a payment in order to score, because that would move real inventory and real money. The module sits armed and closes when the work happens on shift, on its own.

2.body: The tour highlights the actual element and still lets you click it, changes screen when a step calls for it, and survives navigation. If a required step cannot find its element it stops, rather than pointing at nothing.

trust.title: Teaching is the easy half; knowing who can work alone is the other one
trust.body: On your team screen each person shows the percentage of what their own role is expected to know, not a generic syllabus and not a comparison with their colleagues. There is no leaderboard and no ranking, and someone who has not started yet shows a dash rather than a zero, because not having begun is not the same as having failed. Whether a person is ready to work alone stays your call: the screen gives you what you need to make it.

items.0: It is not a certificate course. There is no exam, no badge and no recertification: there are points and a percentage.
items.1: Only work done after starting a module counts. Earlier work is not inherited, so an account that changes hands does not carry over what someone else learned.
items.2: Four kinds of real work are verified: booking created, hand-over, return, and a payment recorded by the agent. A payment arriving through the customer portal carries no record of who took it.
items.3: Progress is picked up when the person next opens Ride University, not in real time and not by a background job.
items.4: The walkthrough is launched with a click. It does not fire by itself the first time somebody signs in.

university.included: Included in Ride Fleet Manager at no extra cost, with the whole syllabus in Spanish and English.

gotchas.title: Where people trip
gotchas.intro: Every module closes by teaching the expensive mistake of its own task, under that same heading. These three are verbatim, and they are the best evidence of who wrote the syllabus.

items.0: The photo step feels skippable when the lot is busy. It is the only evidence of the vehicle condition at handover, and at check-in the agent sees those exact photos beside the camera.
items.1: A car sitting on one of your own lots raises no alert. That is a missed check-in, not a missing car: two different problems with two different fixes.
items.2: A booking in the review tray is not an error. It is the system refusing to guess, usually a customer it could not match with confidence.

market.title: Know what the market charges before you set your rates
market.lede: Every night Ride Fleet reads the rental market at your airport, the same prices your customers see when they shop around, and lines them up against your own rate card class by class.

0.body: A nightly sweep collects competitor offers listed on the major booking sites, each one tagged with its rental agency, its pickup date and its vehicle class.

1.body: Every listing is mapped to the same ACRISS class your own fleet uses, so a compact SUV is compared against a compact SUV and not against something else entirely.

2.value: It moves your prices on your terms
2.body: You set a strategy per class, such as landing second cheapest in the market. The system applies changes inside the limit you set and holds anything beyond it for your approval.

guardrail.title: Automation is only worth having if you can rein it in
guardrail.body: Every rule carries a maximum move, 15 percent today, and any suggestion past it waits for your approval instead of going live. Price floors are respected. Nothing changes quietly: each run is logged with what it saw, what it proposed and what it applied.

items.0: It is not real time. The sweep runs once a night, at 4:00 a.m. New York time, and prices do not move during the day.
items.1: It compares three-day rentals. The 7, 14, 30 and 60-day windows are how far ahead the pickup is booked, not how long the rental lasts.
items.2: There is no direct integration with the online travel agencies. The offers arrive through a metasearch engine that already gathers them.
items.3: Each market is set up per airport. San Juan and Los Angeles are the two running today.

market.addon: Billed separately from Ride Fleet Manager.

case.title: Three months, the same fleet, different software
case.body: International Rental Corp operates in Puerto Rico. These are its prepaid sales through online travel agencies from May to July 2026, running Ride Fleet Manager and Market Intelligence, set against the same three months of 2025, when it ran on another system and priced by hand.
case.reading: The interesting part is not the total but that the jump grows every month, which is the signature of a system that sharpens with use rather than a stroke of luck.
case.note: Figures reported by the customer, covering prepaid sales through online travel agencies and not total revenue. Same fleet, same time of year, same market: what changed was the software and the way prices were set. This is one operator's result, not an average and not a promise of what you will get.

head.title: Where we win: operational intelligence
head.aside: The right-hand column doesn't describe any one competitor. It describes the setup we keep finding when we walk into an operator: a rental system, a spreadsheet and a group chat.

modules.title: Toll Bridge and Voz AI run on the same fleet
modules.body: You start with Ride Fleet Manager. When you want tolls billed without chasing statements, you switch on Toll Bridge. When the phone stops keeping up, you switch on your AI reception. Same record, same invoice, same log.

0.desc: The base: bookings, operations and reporting

1.name: Toll Bridge
1.desc: Tolls reconciled and billed on their own

2.name: Voz AI
2.desc: Your AI reception, answered in Spanish or English

0.q: Do I have to run both business models?
0.a: No. Most operators start with one. What you avoid is having to migrate systems the day you start offering loaners: the new model switches on over the fleet you already have loaded.

1.q: How do AutoExpreso tolls reach the right customer?
1.a: Every crossing carries a plate and a timestamp. Ride Fleet Manager finds which booking held that unit at that moment and assigns the charge, even when the statement arrives three weeks after the customer returned the car. Toll Bridge does the same with SunPass for Florida operators.

2.q: What happens to the data I already have?
2.a: We load fleet, customers and active bookings before you go live. Whatever we can't migrate automatically, we tell you up front on the implementation call — not after you sign.

3.q: Is the interface genuinely in Spanish?
3.a: Yes, and not as an afterthought translation. The system is bilingual to the core: the employee screen, the customer portal, the agreements and the emails all come out in the language the person picks. It was built in Puerto Rico, where that isn't an optional feature.

4.a: That it's in active development and you can't use it in production yet. We don't show it in the demo as if it had shipped, and we don't put it in a contract as if it had. If your decision depends on one of those pieces, say so on the call and we'll give you the real date.

5.q: Do you work outside Puerto Rico?
5.a: Yes. The product was built here and runs here, and it's ready for operators on the US mainland — starting with the markets where SunPass and bilingual operations matter.

6.q: Is there an iOS and Android app?
6.a: Under construction. Ride Fleet Manager runs in the phone and tablet browser today, which is where the counter actually works: the hand-over, the eight photos and the signature are all built for touch. Native apps come after that, and we are not putting a date on it until we have one we can keep.

partner.body: We're early and we say so plainly: instead of inventing testimonials, we'd rather work closely with a handful of operators who want a hand in how this gets built. In exchange, you set the roadmap priority.
